big_idea: A MAP shows places from above. We use SYMBOLS for objects.
learning_intention: We are learning to make a simple map of a familiar place.
student_learning_goal: I can make a simple map of a familiar place.
success_criteria: I can use SYMBOLS for objects.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Symmy and Flippy — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.

minds_on.hook: Flippy: A MAP shows our classroom from ABOVE. The desk is a square. The door is a rectangle. The carpet is a circle! Symmy + Flippy open: 'Top-down, top-down, that's how MAPS look!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Symmy and Flippy puppets. 'Friends — yesterday congruence. Today we make a MAP.'

Introduce vocabulary. Write MAP on chart. 'Map = a drawing of a place from ABOVE — like a bird looking down. We use SYMBOLS for objects.'

Demonstrate. Show classroom. Walk to a desk. 'From above, the desk looks like a SQUARE.' Draw on chart.

Walk to door. 'From above, the door is a RECTANGLE on the wall.' Draw.

Walk to carpet. 'A CIRCLE.' Draw.

Now the windows. 'Long thin rectangles on the side.'

More symbols:
- Bookshelf = long rectangle.
- Round table = circle.
- Whiteboard = wide rectangle on wall.
- Tree (outside) = green dot or circle.
- Path = thin line.

'Flippy says — every object becomes a SHAPE on the map. We pick simple symbols.'

Label each object. 'Don't forget LABELS so others can read the map.'

Demo a finished map. 'Title: My Classroom. Symbols: 20 small squares (desks), 1 rectangle (door), 1 circle (carpet), labels.'

'Today YOU map a place — your bedroom, kitchen, or backyard.'

steps.instruction: Whole group: map our classroom together.
Three stations. A: Read 3 maps and identify objects. B: Map a small space (bedroom). C: Map the schoolyard.
Stretch at C: include compass rose (N/S/E/W).
Discuss bird's-eye view. 'Maps show TOP DOWN, not front.'
steps.teacher_prompt: Show: side view vs top view.

steps.instruction: STRATEGY COMPARE: Two pairs share their bedroom maps and compare how they chose symbols. Cite Liben & Downs (1989) perspective-taking — top-down is the math convention.
steps.teacher_prompt: Symmy: 'Different symbols, same TOP-DOWN view. The MATH cares about the perspective.'

differentiation.for_emerging: Stay at A. Read pre-made maps.
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Walk the classroom; map as you walk. NO-PAPER VERSION: children walk a small classroom zone and SAY their route from above ('I am at the door, then I go to the carpet, then to the bookshelf').

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Three signals: draws from above; uses symbols; labels.

consolidation.exit_routine: Symmy + Flippy map refrain — 'Top-down, top-down, that's how MAPS look!' Class chants 3x. Each child shows their map and names one symbol + label.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child draws SIDE VIEW instead of TOP DOWN — repairing the perspective trap at Grade 2
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On map-making, the Grade-2 trap is perspective confusion: child draws the map from a side view (their own height) instead of top-down (Liben & Downs 1989, 'Children's Understanding of Maps'; Battista on spatial perspective-taking). Without top-down perspective, Lesson 5's capstone mirror-maze cannot ground.

Yesterday Lesson 3 worked on congruence. Today: top-down maps. Lesson 5 capstones.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Pair at B. Child drawing a 'map' of bedroom. Drawing a bed with headboard, footboard, blanket — side view, not top.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Beautiful drawing! But Flippy asks — what would your bed look like if you were a BIRD looking DOWN?'

Guide. 'From above, you'd just see the rectangle of the mattress. No headboard. Top view.'

Draw a top-view bed. 'Now this is map-style.'

Generlise. 'Symmy says — maps are TOP DOWN. We see the FOOTPRINT of objects, not the side.'

If still side-viewing: provide a top-down photo example. 'Like this picture from a drone.'
common_misconceptions: Side view OK on map. (Repair: top down only.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child draws side-view: physical demo with toys + phone camera held above; child sees the top-down view.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child draws top-down but misses scale: drill 'big things take MORE map space than small things.'
DIAGNOSTIC C — child draws but uses random symbols: drill the key — 'every symbol gets a label.'

parts_outline.task: Look at a map. Identify 4 objects.
Map a place at home. Add labels.
